name: medium-mstp-pair-root-reboot-secondary
title: MLAG secondary reboot · Medium lab, MSTP, MLAG pair as root
action: Resets all three bridges over management SSH with protocol-mode=mstp, priority 0x1000 on CHR 1 and CHR 2 and 0x8000 on the access switch. It requires a loss-free baseline with root ID 0x1000.02:00:00:21:00:11 in the access switch's BPDUs. It then reboots CHR 2 (MLAG secondary) with `/system reboot`, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

witness.name: dc1-access-switch1
witness.role: Dual-attached access switch and external RSTP root candidate

c1.name: dc1-traffic-host1
c1.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 1

c2.name: dc1-traffic-host2
c2.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 2

phases.name: Secondary down
phases.expected: CHR 1 keeps the shared system ID, which is both the RSTP bridge ID and the LACP system ID, so the access switch still sees root 0x1000.02:00:00:21:00:11 and its uplink stays the forwarding root port. The virtual links keep carrier, so the access switch and traffic host 2 drop their member to CHR 2 at the LACP short timeout (3 × 1 s). Only traffic hashed to that member sees brief loss.

phases.name: Secondary back
phases.expected: CHR 2 keeps its bond members out of the bond until the MLAG system ID syncs (mlag-init-delay), then adds them under the unchanged shared system ID. The root ID and the access switch's forwarding uplink do not change, so loss is brief or none.
